findings.who: A policyholder receives fixed daily or monthly benefits under a contract that is not a qualified LTC contract. The insurer's Form 1099-LTC has the "Qualified contract" box in box 4 checked anyway, or the contract was issued before 1997 and was later changed materially, so it lost grandfathered status while the issuer kept checking the box.
findings.why_no: The question asks only whether box 4 is left unchecked on the form. The box is checked, so the truthful answer is no, even though the contract is not qualified.
findings.line: f8853c.nonqualified_if_periodic (and through it line 18, which then wrongly equals line 17)
findings.irs_text: i8853 (2025) p. 8: a qualified contract issued before January 1, 1997 is one that "met state law requirements ... and hasn't been changed materially"; f8853 (2025) p. 2, line 17 Caution: "Don’t use lines 18 through 26 to figure the taxable amount of benefits paid under an LTC insurance contract that isn’t a qualified LTC insurance contract"
findings.fix: Ask about the contract, not the form: "Was any of these payments made under a contract that is not a qualified long-term care insurance contract? Box 4 of Form 1099-LTC usually shows this, but a contract issued before 1997 that was materially changed later, or a contract the insurer says doesn't meet section 7702B, is not qualified even if the box is checked."

findings.who: A filer receives fixed periodic LTC benefits under a nonqualified contract, but the Form 1099-LTC leaves the "Per diem" box in box 3 unchecked, the payments came with no Form 1099-LTC at all (for example, from a foreign insurer), or the form shows "Reimbursed amount" by mistake.
findings.why_no: The parent helper for line 17 follows the form's per diem box, so the filer answers no to "payments were made at a set rate." Line 17 becomes 0, the gate is false, and the nonqualified-contract question is never asked. The refusal or Schedule 1 reporting that the line 17 Caution requires is lost.
findings.irs_text: i8853 (2025) p. 8: "Per diem payments are payments of a fixed amount made on a periodic basis without regard to actual expenses incurred. Box 3 of Form 1099-LTC should indicate whether payments were per diem payments."
findings.fix: Ask the parent as a fact: "Did you receive any long-term care benefits paid as a fixed amount per day, week, or month, regardless of your actual costs, whether or not a Form 1099-LTC checks the Per diem box?" Also ask about nonqualified contracts for any LTC benefit, not only when line 17 is more than zero.

findings.who: Spouses file jointly, and the spouse is the policyholder of a nonqualified LTC contract paying per diem benefits for a parent or for the spouse.
findings.why_no: If the line 17 helper or the box 4 question is worded as "you received" or "your forms," the filer answers for themselves only. Line 17 and the gated question then cover only the filer's own Section C.
findings.irs_text: i8853 (2025) p. 8: "The policyholder is required to report the income, even if payment is assigned to a third party or parties." f8853 (2025) p. 2: "If more than one Section C is attached, check here"
findings.fix: Ask per policyholder and per insured: "Did you or your spouse, as policyholder, receive ...", and repeat the box 4 question for each Section C.

findings.who: A filer whose per diem forms include accelerated death benefits paid periodically under a life insurance policy for a chronically ill insured. Those forms leave box 4 unchecked because the payer is not an LTC contract.
findings.why_no: The question does not say which forms "those forms" means, so the filer counts the life insurance form. They answer yes, the interview ends, and the line 19 path is wrongly refused. A filer who instead excludes these forms may also wonder whether the question applies to them at all.
findings.irs_text: i8853 (2025) p. 8: "Accelerated death benefits paid with respect to an insured individual who is chronically ill are generally excludable from your gross income to the same extent as they would be under a qualified LTC insurance contract." Line 19: "These amounts are generally shown in box 2 of Form 1099-LTC."
findings.fix: Limit the question to forms with an amount in box 1 that came from a long-term care insurance contract. In the help, say that box 4 is left blank on accelerated death benefit forms and that this does not count.

findings.who: Any filer reading the help "Box 4 of Form 1099-LTC is checked 'Qualified contract' for most policies."
findings.why_no: The help suggests the answer is usually no and invites a filer to answer from that assumption without looking at the box or the contract.
findings.irs_text: f8853 (2025) p. 2, line 18: "Enter the part of the amount on line 17 that is from qualified LTC insurance contracts"
findings.fix: Replace the help with: "Check box 4 on each form, and your policy documents, before answering."

findings.who: Filer with a qualified LTC contract first issued before August 1, 1996, later exchanged or modified after July 31, 1996 to increase per diem payments, who received 2025 reimbursements for qualified LTC services and has no other line 24 reimbursements. The filer reads the general pre-1996 exclusion and enters zero for line 24.
findings.why_no: The instructions say 'Generally, don't include on line 24 reimbursements ... under a contract issued before August 1, 1996'; the filer stops there and misses the later sentence requiring inclusion after a post-July 31, 1996 modification to increase per diem.
findings.irs_text: i8853 p. 9, Line 24: 'However, you must include reimbursements if the contract was exchanged or modified after July 31, 1996, to increase per diem payments or reimbursements.'
findings.fix: Put the exchange/modification exception in the line 24 help and gate; do not treat all pre-August 1, 1996 contracts as excluded when the contract was modified after July 31, 1996 to increase per diem.

findings.who: Filer with a pre-1996 contract modified after July 31, 1996 to increase per diem, and qualified LTC services in 2025; the insurer has approved reimbursement but has not paid it by the filing date. The filer has no other line 24 reimbursements and enters zero because no reimbursement has been received.
findings.why_no: The form line asks for 'Reimbursements' and the filer reads that as money actually received, not amounts expected to be received.
findings.irs_text: i8853 p. 9, Line 24: 'Enter the reimbursements you received or expect to receive through insurance or otherwise for qualified LTC services provided for the insured for LTC periods in 2025.'
findings.fix: State 'received or expected to be received for 2025 LTC periods' in the line 24 help and ask that before computing the gate.

findings.who: Filer with a pre-1996 contract modified after July 31, 1996 to increase per diem; the insurer paid the nursing home directly and sent no reimbursement check to the filer. The filer has no other line 24 reimbursements and answers zero because they received no money.
findings.why_no: The form line says 'Reimbursements for qualified LTC services provided for the insured'; the filer reads this as money paid to them, not payments made on their behalf to a provider.
findings.irs_text: i8853 p. 9, Line 24: 'Enter the reimbursements you received or expect to receive through insurance or otherwise for qualified LTC services provided for the insured for LTC periods in 2025.'
findings.fix: Ask about reimbursements paid to the provider or on the insured's behalf, not only checks received by the filer.

findings.who: Married couple filing jointly; the spouse, not the filer, received the only reimbursements for qualified LTC services under a pre-1996 contract modified after July 31, 1996 to increase per diem. The filer answers for themselves only and enters zero.
findings.why_no: The line 20/line 24 helper says 'you' and not 'you or your spouse'; the filer reads it as asking only about their own receipts.
findings.irs_text: i8853 p. 9, Filing Requirements for Section C: 'Did you (or your spouse, if filing jointly) receive payments in 2025 made on a per diem or other periodic basis under an LTC insurance contract?'
findings.fix: On a joint return, use 'you or your spouse' for line 20, line 24, and the pre-1996 contract question.

findings.who: Filer received the only reimbursements for qualified LTC services provided to a dependent parent under a pre-1996 contract modified after July 31, 1996 to increase per diem. The filer thinks Section C applies only to the filer's or spouse's own LTC and enters zero.
findings.why_no: Line 24 says 'for the insured,' but the filer reads the section as being about 'you' and does not complete it for another insured person.
findings.irs_text: i8853 p. 9, Filing Requirements for Section C: 'Go through this chart for each insured person for whom you received long-term care (LTC) payments.'
findings.fix: Say 'for any insured person, including a dependent or other individual, for whom you received LTC payments' in the line 24 and pre-1996 questions.

findings.who: Filer with a pre-1996 contract modified after July 31, 1996 to increase per diem, reimbursed by the insurer for qualified LTC services but issued no Form 1099-LTC. The filer has no other line 24 reimbursements and answers zero because no form was received.
findings.why_no: The line 24 help mentions Form 1099-LTC box 3; the filer treats a 1099 as the trigger and says no when none arrived.
findings.irs_text: i8853 p. 9, Line 24: 'Box 3 of Form 1099-LTC should indicate if payments were made on a reimbursement basis.'
findings.fix: Ask about the fact of reimbursement, not receipt of Form 1099-LTC; a 1099 is not a condition for line 24.

findings.who: A filer who received only accelerated death benefits on a per diem basis that were not paid on behalf of a chronically ill individual, so line 20 is zero because line 19 excludes them, and another person received set-rate LTC payments for the same insured. If the insured was not terminally ill, line 15 is Yes and Multiple Payees requires a statement.
findings.why_no: The computed gate tests only line 20 > 0; with no amount in line 18 or 19 the tool treats line 15 as No and never asks it, even though the Section C filing chart requires line 15 in the limited Section C for accelerated death benefits not paid for a chronically ill individual.
findings.irs_text: i8853 p. 9, Filing Requirements for Section C: 'Complete only lines 14a, 14b, 15, 16, 17 (if applicable), and 26 of Section C'; i8853 p. 9, Multiple Payees: 'In all other cases in which you checked “Yes” on line 15, attach a statement duplicating lines 18 through 26.'
findings.fix: Ask line 15 whenever any Section C is required, not only when line 20 > 0. Include the limited Section C branch for accelerated death benefits where line 20 may be zero, and then apply the Multiple Payees special rules.

findings.who: A chronically ill insured has life-insurance accelerated death benefits paid periodically and reported in box 2 of Form 1099-LTC, while box 3 does not show 'Per diem' or the filer reads the gate as limited to care-cost payments.
findings.why_no: The gate points only to box 3 'Per diem' and to payments made 'whatever the care cost'; the filer has no LTC care-cost per diem/box 3 check, so answers no.
findings.irs_text: i8853 p. 8, Line 19: 'Enter the total accelerated death benefits you received with respect to the insured listed on line 14a. These amounts are generally shown in box 2 of Form 1099-LTC. Include only amounts you received while the insured was a chronically ill individual.'
findings.fix: Broaden the gate to ask about accelerated death benefits on a per diem or other periodic basis shown in box 2, including while chronically ill and excluding terminally ill amounts, without requiring box 3 'Per diem' or care costs.

findings.who: A filer receives accelerated death benefits on an 'other periodic basis' but the amount is not a fixed set amount per day, week, or month, so the filer cannot say yes to 'a set amount per ... period.'
findings.why_no: The gate asks only for a set amount per period; the filer's periodic accelerated death benefits varied, so they truthfully answer no.
findings.irs_text: f8853 (2025) p. 2, line 19: 'Accelerated death benefits received on a per diem or other periodic basis'; i8853 p. 8, Line 19: 'Enter the total accelerated death benefits ... Include only amounts you received while the insured was a chronically ill individual.'
findings.fix: Ask about accelerated death benefits on a per diem or other periodic basis, not only fixed set-amount payments.

findings.who: A filer receives qualified LTC per diem benefits that were less than or equal to the actual cost of care, so the filer believes the payments merely reimbursed care costs.
findings.why_no: The gate help says 'Payments that only repaid care costs are not taxed: answer No,' which the filer reads as covering per diem benefits that did not exceed care costs.
findings.irs_text: f8853 (2025) p. 1, line 17: 'Enter the total of the amounts from box 1 of all Forms 1099-LTC you received with respect to the insured on which the Per diem box in box 3 is checked'; i8853 p. 8 defines per diem as fixed periodic payments 'without regard to actual expenses incurred.'
findings.fix: Limit the reimbursement shortcut to box 3 'Reimbursed amount' forms and state that a box 3 'Per diem' form still requires the box 1 gross amount even if the benefits did not exceed care costs.

findings.who: A filer's per diem LTC benefits are paid by the insurer directly to a nursing home or other care provider, so the filer never receives the check.
findings.why_no: The gate asks 'Were any payments...' and the filer reads that as payments to them, answering no because the payments went straight to the provider.
findings.irs_text: i8853 p. 8, Policyholder: 'The policyholder is required to report the income, even if payment is assigned to a third party or parties'; f8853 line 17 includes box 1 amounts on forms with 'Per diem' checked.
findings.fix: Word the gate as payments to the filer or for this person, including payments sent directly to a care provider, and include the assigned-payment rule in the gate help.
